symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by one or more major depressive episodes in which delusions and/or hallucinations are present and are typically mood-congruent with the person's pervasive negative themes of guilt, worthlessness, or doom. The psychotic features occur only during episodes of major depression and are not better explained by a primary psychotic disorder such as schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. Clinically, it often presents with profound functional impairment, high suicide risk, and may have a more prolonged or recurrent course than non-psychotic depression. It is distinguished from severe non-psychotic depression by the presence of fixed false beliefs or perceptual disturbances and from bipolar disorder by the absence of manic or hypomanic episodes.

patient.personality: He is a disciplined, data‑driven sales leader with a strong solitary streak, who unwinds through art, music, and late‑night creative pursuits.
patient.stressor: Roughly 16 months ago, Peter’s company underwent a major restructuring after losing a key contract, and he was tasked with salvaging an underperforming sales division while his own compensation became heavily tied to aggressive new targets. As market conditions worsened despite his efforts, he began spending longer hours alone in the office poring over analytics and forecasts, quietly internalizing the business downturn as a personal failure that jeopardized his family’s financial security and future. Over the following year, he gradually gave up his usual hiking and museum visits, fixated on worst‑case financial scenarios, and started to interpret neutral market news and minor household expenses as ominous signs that he was leading his family toward inevitable ruin. When he found himself repeatedly contemplating that his wife and children would be better off without him and began making concrete mental plans about not being around if the next quarter went badly, his wife noticed his late-night isolation at the piano and convinced him, with the support of his primary care physician, to see a psychiatrist.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep thinking my family would be better off if I just didn’t wake up anymore, and those thoughts are getting harder to push away.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Over the past year I've become absolutely convinced that the downturn in our numbers isn’t just bad luck—that I somehow triggered it, like every missed sale and layoff in the division is my fault and the bank and the IRS are quietly circling my family because they know I’ve ruined our future, even though everyone keeps telling me that’s irrational and there’s no evidence of it anywhere in the statements or reports I obsess over.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m alone late at night in my home office or at the piano, I hear this low, clear voice right behind me saying things like, “You’ve bankrupted them,” or “They’d be better off if you were gone,” and sometimes I see dark shapes moving in the corners of the room that feel like debt collectors or some kind of judgment coming for me, even though I know logically there’s nothing there.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest like a weight pressing me into the mattress, and I just move through the day numb and hopeless, thinking, “What’s the point?” whether I’m in a meeting, driving home, or sitting at the dinner table with my kids.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I’ll lie in bed staring at the ceiling until two or three in the morning running numbers in my head, then wake up again at four or five with my heart racing and my mind jumping straight back to worst‑case scenarios, so even on nights when I technically get enough hours, I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept at all.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: My wife says it’s like I’m moving in slow motion now—just shuffling from room to room, staring at emails for minutes before clicking anything, taking forever to answer simple questions—and when I’m at my lowest, I catch myself just sitting at my desk or the piano bench, hands still, unable to make myself start even the smallest task.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I walk around with this constant, crushing sense that I’m a fraud and a failure as a provider, that I’ve destroyed my family’s security, and I replay every minor decision—like buying my son a new pair of shoes or taking the kids to a museum years ago—as proof that I’ve been reckless and selfish and deserve to be punished for what I’ve done to them.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: For months now, whenever I look at the quarterly projections or even at my kids’ college brochures, my mind jumps to very specific ideas about how I could just not be here anymore—like driving into a concrete barrier on my commute or taking a bottle of pills from the medicine cabinet—and I catch myself planning out the details and timing so that my wife and children could collect the insurance and finally be free of the burden of me.
